about: Proposed initial-condition / object values for the serve_bread simulator, from the real evidence (human training data: 60 Aria episodes measured with SLAM-triangulated keypoints, masks and semidense points; real rollout videos; real code/config). Owners: robustness session (sampling.py, scene config), physics session (bread model). See simulation/docs/real_vs_sim.md section 3. Each entry: current sim value, proposed value, evidence, confidence.

cam_height.evidence: Two full-resolution front-view frames with the arms folded at home (website serve_bread.mp4 last frame, cross_condition_3.mp4 first frame): camera-above-arm-base / arm-base-above-table = 398/271 and 330/225 px = 1.47 at nearly the same depth. Hand-eye calibration puts the D405 0.221 m above the bases, so bases ~0.15 m (0.14-0.16 with perspective) above the table and the camera ~0.37 m. The current 0.215 m base height is an inference from the Control.yaml comment that safe_z_min = -0.20 'protects the table'.
cam_height.impact: single-arm production success, paper protocol, seed 7777, 40 scenes, by cam_height: 0.436 -> 12.5 %, 0.396 -> 40 %, 0.366 -> 67.5 %, 0.346 -> 75 %, 0.336 -> 75 %; bimanual production at 0.366: 56.2 % per arm (0.436: 40.6 %); tuned single 85 % (82.5 %), tuned bimanual 79.7 % (92.2 %; tuned at 0.436, re-tune needed)
cam_height.confidence: medium: pixel ratio from a monocular third-person view; confirm with the first real log (replay_real.py fits the table plane in the logged D405 depth: camera height above the table directly)

extents_cm.evidence: human data, 60 episodes: length 14.5 +- 0.4 (mask silhouette; contour+erosion agrees), width 7.1 +- 0.8 (mask, corrected for side-view inflation), height 5.4 median (semidense p95). The sim size came from the inner-eroded contour (~4 px per side smaller). One croissant type in all 61 episodes.
extents_cm.confidence: length high, height medium, width medium (correction model)

scale_if_uniform.note: scene.bread.right.scale (uniform, same density, landed on main 22ede5e): 1.05 matches the length, 1.18 the width; 1.06 is the compromise. A non-uniform (x 1.05, y 1.15, z 1.08) bread_gen change would match all three.

mass_g.proposed: keep 50 g (real weight, README); with uniform scale the sim scales mass by scale^3, so set density to keep 50 g if scale is changed

bread_danish.note: Not in the human data (robot rollouts only). Current 14.0 x 7.4 x 6.0 cm was measured against the plate in the rollout video; no new evidence.

layout_single_paper_protocol.paper: bread-plate horizontal offset U[0, 50] cm, depths randomized independently, right arm starts from an 'arbitrary, non-aligned pose above the bread' (CoRL App. Task Details). Real Control.yaml however has go_initial_pose: True (fixed start).
layout_single_paper_protocol.current_sim: gap (y) 0.16-0.38 m, plate x 0.40-0.54, bread x 0.39-0.55, yaw 55-125 deg, fixed start pose
layout_single_paper_protocol.human_data: bread-plate distance 27.9 cm (22.2-31.4), plate straight left of the bread (direction 89 deg, 74-110), bread yaw 86 deg (67-101)

proposed.note: widen towards the paper's [0, 50] cm offset where physically possible (bread and plate do not overlap below ~0.17 m centre distance with the 24.5 cm plate; the paper's 0 cm presumably means front-back offset). Keep yaw 90 +- 35. Optional start-pose noise (+-5 cm EE, +-10 deg) to cover 'arbitrary start'.

layout_single_paper_protocol.confidence: low: paper text only, no measured real positions

layout_vs_training_distribution.finding: At t0 (first training frame) the human objects are closer to the camera and lower in the image than the sim's: bread forward of the camera foot 36 +- 4 cm (30-44) vs sim 39-55 (78 % of human episodes closer than the sim minimum); bread depth along the optical axis 53 +- 4 vs 62 +- 4 cm; bread 14.5 +- 3.6 deg below the optical axis vs 4.3 deg (88 % of human episodes lower in the image than any sim draw); only 2 of 60 human layouts fall inside the single-arm sampler on all axes at once. Head camera height 43.7 +- 3.7 cm (three scene groups 46 / 42 / 38) and pitch 34.3 +- 3.5 deg vs the sim's fixed 43.6 cm / 37 deg.
layout_vs_training_distribution.proposed: Add an in-distribution diagnostic set next to the default sampler: bread x 0.29-0.45 m in the sim world (check the arm's reach; at x = 0.30 the bread is still in view, ~17 deg below the axis), bread-plate sideways gap 0.21-0.31 m (human 26.7 +- 3.0 cm), forward offset 0 +- 0.06 m, bread yaw 87 +- 10 deg; keep the current wide ranges as the out-of-distribution test (18 % of sim gaps are < 20 cm, never seen in the human data; at 16 cm the croissant touches the plate rim). Compare against the human data in single mode (bimanual puts the bread ~12 cm further right).
layout_vs_training_distribution.confidence: high for the human numbers; the robot-side implication is a hypothesis
